GALWAY COUNTY COUNCIL GAELTACHT SCHOLARSHIPS 2026 UPDATE 
Galway County Council is pleased to present an update on the 2026 Gaeltacht Scholarship 
Programme. The initiative continues to support second-level students from functional areas 
of the Council in developing their Irish-language proficiency and deepening their 
understanding of Irish culture through attendance at recognised Gaeltacht summer colleges. 
EXPANSION OF THE SCHOLARSHIP PROGRAMME FOR 2026 
The Council has expanded the programme significantly: 
•

2025 to 27 in 2026, representing a substantial enhancement of the scheme. 
• 
Additional Gaeltacht College Partner: Galway County Council is delighted to welcome 
Coláiste na bFhiann, Rosmuc as a new partner college for 2026, bringing the total 
number of participating colleges to nine.

LOCAL ENHANCEMENT PROGRAMME 2026  
Galway County Council has received funding of €213,600 from the Department of Rural and 
Community Development and the Gaeltacht under the Local Enhancement Programme 
2026.  This fund will provide capital funding to support community groups across Ireland. 
  
The funding will support groups, particularly in disadvantaged areas to carry out necessary 
repairs and improvements to their facilities, purchase equipment such as tables and chairs, 
tools and signage, laptops and printers, training equipment, and improving energy efficiency 
of community facilities to reduce ongoing costs.  
This year’s programme places particular focus on designated Community Support Centres 
following Storm Eowyn in January 2025, when many rural areas of Galway were left without 
electricity for extended periods. Groups are invited to apply for funding to help purchase a 
generator, as well as for the supply and installation of a changeover switch, enabling the use 
of a county-owned mobile generator to maintain essential services during future 
disruptions. 
In line with previous years, the LCDC will endeavour to allocate 30% of this fund towards 
small grants of €1,000 or less to maximise its benefit to small grassroots groups.  
 
This funding is now open for applications with a closing date of 23rd February 2026. Funding 
recommendations of the LCDC will be submitted to the Department of Rural and 
Community Development and the Gaeltacht by the end of March 2026, for funding 
announcements by the Minister for Rural & Community Development & Gaeltacht in May 
2026.   All capital projects will be required to be completed and grants drawn down by end 
of October 2026.  
  
Applicants should apply via our online grants system at https://galwaycoco.submit.com/ 
HEALTHY IRELAND 
Healthy County Galway 
enters 2025 with a 
continued commitment to 
enhance health and 
wellbeing initiatives across the county. The LCDC Health & Wellbeing Sub-Committee will

12 
 
meet in January to finalise the proposed workplan for the 2025 Healthy Ireland Fund 
allocation. The year ahead will see Healthy County Galway implementing a number of 
initiatives focused on improving health and wellbeing outcomes at local level. Our flagship 
programmes for 2025 focused on farmer wellbeing, women’s health, and dementia 
supports with this work extending 2026, with further plans to expand, tailor, and sustain 
progress through partnerships with key local, community, and statutory partners. 
The Dementia Café initiative in Connemara will continue to focus on 
sustaining existing cafés while incorporating additional activities 
and making full use of the activity packs provided in 2025. 
Planning is already underway for two launches in 2026 under the 
Understand Together campaign, in partnership with the HSE and 
key stakeholders. These launches will seek to raise awareness of 
dementia within the Connemara region and actively involve the 
local community. The campaign will include community engagement 
events, information sessions, and promotional activities to encourage participation and 
understanding. By embedding the Understand Together message into these cafés, we aim to 
foster a culture of empathy and inclusion while promoting positive social connections for 
those affected by dementia. 
While the rollout of social digital hubs experienced delays in 2025, implementation is 
planned to continue in 2026 in partnership with local libraries and Age Friendly Galway. 
These hubs will provide digital skills training for individuals aged 50+, supporting the Healthy 
Galway objective of increasing social and leisure opportunities for older adults while 
promoting digital literacy and social connection. 
A further allocation will be available for community-led projects under the Healthy Galway 
program. These initiatives provide opportunities for social engagement, skill development, 
and improved physical and mental health, contributing to the overall wellbeing of 
communities across the county. 
In partnership with local agencies, Healthy County Galway will 
also apply for the Period Poverty Fund under Galway County 
Council. This initiative aims to install sanitary product 
dispensers in public facilities in the county and provide free 
sanitary products to those in need. In addition, educational 
resources and informational sessions for women will be 
delivered, supporting the sexual health priority theme. 
Collaboration with agencies will ensure key areas for 
distribution are identified, enabling equitable access and reducing barriers to essential 
health products. 
Another key focus for Healthy County Galway in 2025 will be to support the Western Region 
Drug and Alcohol Task Force Recovery Strategy 2025–2030. This commitment aims to assist 
individuals in recovery and their families by encouraging engagement in positive activities

13 
 
within their communities. Through collaboration with local partners, Healthy County Galway 
will support participation in new social and leisure opportunities that foster inclusion and 
wellbeing.  
Further to this, Healthy County Galway will engage with marginalised groups, particularly 
the Traveller community, applying an evidence-based, community-led approach to increase 
social and leisure activities in a culturally sensitive manner that meets the needs of the 
community. These actions demonstrate a continued emphasis on reducing health 
inequalities and encouraging meaningful participation for all. 
Over the coming period, Healthy County Galway will continue to build partnerships, sustain 
core programmes into 2026, and prioritise sustainability and inclusivity in all initiatives while 
aligning with national health priorities under the Healthy Ireland Framework. 
COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT AND SOCIAL INCLUSION 
We continue to progress the establishment of Community Support Centres (CSCs) across the 
county, following lessons learned during Storm Éowyn in early 2025. These centres are 
intended to provide safe, supportive environments during severe weather events or 
prolonged service disruptions, offering essential facilities such as water, hot food, phone 
charging, broadband access, and toilet facilities. 
The Expression of Interest (EOI) process launched on 12 December 2025 remains open on a 
rolling basis. As of January 2026, 63 responses have been received from community groups 
and facility operators. The aim is to formalize a network of designated centres comparable 
to the informal arrangements that proved effective during previous emergencies. Centres 
that do not currently meet all requirements are encouraged to address gaps and re-submit 
their EOI. 
The 52 Community Support Centres that have been successful in their Expression of Interest 
submissions have now been formally designated and are listed on the Galway County 
Council website(https://www.galway.ie/en/community-tourism-arts/community-
development/community-support-centres). This ensures transparency and allows 
communities to easily identify their nearest centre in the event of an emergency. We aim to 
reach out to designated CSCs and elected officials with formalised operating procedures, as 
agreed by members of the Major Emergency Development Committee, prior to the next 
convening of the Committee. 
Work is underway to confirm three priority centres for funded rewiring to facilitate mobile 
generator use. This is in response to CCMA guidance and the need for resilience during 
prolonged outages. These measures will ensure hubs, identified based on geographic 
coverage and vulnerability criteria, are adequately equipped to serve vulnerable individuals 
and meet operational standards. 
In addition, Galway County Council will receive mobile generators as part of a national 
initiative to create a shared pool of mobile units. These four generators will be available for

14 
 
deployment to CSCs during severe weather events or other emergencies, providing a 
flexible backup solution where permanent installations are not yet in place. 
Community Support Centres that are not in receipt of dedicated funding under the current 
allocation can avail of support through the Local Enhancement Programme (LEP) 2026. This 
funding stream may be used to cover essential infrastructure upgrades such as rewiring 
works to facilitate generator installation and/or the purchase of generators. Centres are 
encouraged to review LEP eligibility criteria and submit applications to strengthen their 
capacity for emergency response and community resilience. Applications will open on from 
14th January 2026 and close on 23rd February 2026.

PORTUMA TOWN HALL, TVRS2025 
The Minister for Rural and Community Development and the Gaeltacht, Dara Calleary, in 
December confirmed that all seven applications submitted by Galway County Council under 
the Town and Village Renewal Scheme for 2025 have been approved for funding. 
The single largest allocation, €500,000, has been granted for the upgrade of the historic 
Bridewell jail behind Portumna Courthouse along with planned improvements to Portumna 
Town Hall. 
Killimor has been awarded €214,550 and Ahascragh €250,000 to support continuing efforts 
to tackle vacancy and dereliction. Both communities in East Galway are already part of the 
council’s first Compulsory Purchase Order Activation Programme for vacant properties. 
Comhairle Ceantar na nOileán in Leitir Móir will receive €300,000 to enhance Páirc Pobal 
and develop a new playground. A further €300,000 has been approved for improvements to 
the Ionad Pobail facility in An Fhairce Clonbur to meet growing demand for local meeting 
space. 
In Corofin, €45,572 has been allocated for a community feasibility study aimed at identifying 
new village-centre amenities. Athenry will receive €42,750 to advance proposals for 
additional community meeting space identified through the town team process.

are already underway. In 2025 and 2024, Galway County 
Council was successful in securing a total of €18,000 in 
additional funding to run a full programme of events as Gaeilge 
on all three Aran Islands. We are currently in the process of 
developing our proposal and budget to apply for the funding 
again in 2026.  
Meanwhile on the mainland, the Open Call for funding launched 
on Tuesday the 13th of January. The grants for Cruinniú na nÓg 
are generally small, with a max amount of €750. Youth groups, artists, schools, and sports 
clubs are encouraged to apply to put on a free event for young people on the 6th of June.

language. It is hoped that 2026 will continue to grow on the successes of previous years as 
we bring creativity to every child in County Galway.

groups in both libraries to design and produce a stunning tapestry that honours Irish 
creatives, local heroes, and the surrounding landscape. Through stitching and weaving, 
participants explored Ireland’s cultural heritage and fostered dialogue through shared 
artistry—creating something deeply personal and profoundly communal.

music to reflect the rich landscape and heritage of the Westside community. Gerry’s

tapestry. Her words ‘Spools of thought across the table, hands move steady, sure as breath, 
The room begins in conversation, then settles to the sound of thread’ carry the echo of 
conversations, the hum of creativity and the heartbeat of community. Additional creative 
contributions that highlight the art and creativity of this tapestry include written pieces by 
Tuam’s own Padraig Stevens and librarian Margaret Garvey, which will be displayed 
alongside the tapestry.  
Designed as a legacy piece, Mapping 1925 will enhance Tuam & Westside Libraries for 
generations to come—a vibrant reminder of how heritage inspires innovation.   
Mapping 1925 reminds us that art is not only about beauty—it is about connection. It 
connects us to our past, to each other, and to the future we are shaping together

A collaborative initiative involving leading regional bodies, including the Department of 
Further and Higher Education, Research, Innovation and Science; the Atlantic Technological 
University, the Western Development Commission, the Regional Skills Forum and the Irish 
Technology & General Skillnet has launched a pivotal report outlining a strategic roadmap 
for integrating Artificial Intelligence (AI) into the small and medium-sized enterprise sector 
across the West of Ireland.  
The report, Powered by AI: Unlocking SME Growth in the West, provides region-specific 
insights and actionable recommendations to help businesses move beyond initial 
experimentation to structured, sustainable AI adoption. This initiative is aligned with the 
broader West Regional Enterprise Plan, ensuring a coordinated approach to digital 
transformation. 
The study, authored by Dr. George Onofrei and Dr. Muslim Jameel Syed of the Atlantic 
Technological University, found a significant appetite for AI adoption, with many SMEs 
already using basic tools for efficiency gains in areas like administration and customer 
engagement. However, key barriers are slowing progress, including skills gaps, regulatory 
uncertainty around the EU AI Act, and a lack of specific funding and technical support. 
In response to these challenges, the report proposes a series of targeted recommendations 
to strengthen the regional ecosystem. These include establishing "test-before-invest" 
demonstration hubs to de-risk pilot projects, funding short "implementation sprints" to 
operationalise AI solutions and creating a central repository of local use-cases. The partners 
also advocate for a two-track modular training approach, offering strategic sessions for 
leadership and hands-on clinics for operational staff, alongside peer-to-peer learning 
networks and mentoring from AI practitioners.

the establishment of an AI compliance helpdesk and improved collaboration among all

The Community Monuments Fund was first established in 2020 to provide investment in 
Ireland’s archaeological heritage. 
Funding is prioritised for local authorities, private owners and custodians and community 
groups for the care, conservation, maintenance, protection and promotion of archaeological 
monuments. 
Total funding available nationally for projects under Community Monuments Fund 2026 will 
be €7,500,000. 
The Community Monuments Fund invests in archaeological heritage and helps owners and 
custodians of archaeological monuments to safeguard them into the future for the benefit 
of communities and the public. 
The impacts of climate change on our monuments is increasingly evident. With increased 
weathering and severe climate events, the repair cycle on built heritage is likely to become 
shorter. Increased maintenance and repair will be key to building resilience in our 
monuments to enable them to withstand the effects of a changing environment. 
CORE AIMS OF THE FUND 
The core aims of this Fund are the conservation, maintenance, protection and presentation 
of archaeological monuments. It will: 
• enable conservation works to be carried out on monuments which are deemed to be 
significant and in need of urgent support 
• build resilience in our monuments to enable them to withstand the effects of climate 
change encourage access to monuments and improve their presentation. 
The Department encourages project promoters to incorporate a traditional skills training 
element in projects. 
STREAMS 1-3 
The Community Monuments Fund has 3 Streams: 
Stream 1 will offer grants up to €100,000 aimed at essential repairs and capital works for 
the conservation and repair of archaeological monuments.

Stream 2 will offer grants of up to €30,000 for development of Conservation Management 
Plans/Reports that are aimed at identifying measures for conservation of archaeological 
monuments and improving public access. 
Stream 3 will offer grants of up to €30,000 for enhancement of access infrastructure and 
interpretation (including virtual/online) at archaeological monuments. 
ELIGIBLE PROJECTS 
The Community Monuments Fund provides funding for projects in relation to: 
Archaeological Monuments that are included in the Record of Monuments and Places (RMP) 
under the National Monuments Act 1930 (as amended) 
Archaeological Monuments that are identified in the Sites and Monuments Record compiled 
by the National Monuments Service. 
Eligible projects will be drawn from the following categories: 
Projects proposed by a Local Authority in relation to archaeological monuments in public 
ownership, where a clear heritage focus and community or public benefit has been 
demonstrated 
Projects proposed by a Local Authority on foot of applications from private applicants who 
are the owners or custodians of relevant archaeological monuments where there is a 
tangible public benefit 
Projects with a clearly defined heritage focus and community or public benefit proposed 
directly to the Department by a State-funded organisation working in the heritage area.
